sentences.text: Keichousaurus is sometimes classified within Nothosauroidea but is more commonly listed as a separate, primitive lineage within Sauropterygia.
This animal possessed a long serpentine neck, a relatively small head, and a long tail.
It is distinguished by its broad ulna, a feature that makes it unlike other European genera.
Keichousaurus lacked a sternum and had paddled-shaped forelimbs, suggesting the forelimbs were crucial for movement.
Most specimens had small bodies, with sexually mature males reaching a snout-vent length of 12.6 cm and females 12.2 cm.
Evidence suggests that Keichousaurus young emerged from their mothers head first.
The holotype of K. hui was discovered in 1957 in Guizhou Province, China, and named by Young in 1958.
The species K. yuananensis was discovered in the Jialingjiang Formation of Hebei, China, and named by Young in 1965 based on a partial skeleton.
Keichousaurus likely used a rowing swimming motion powered by its paddle-like limbs.
Analysis of gut contents suggests Keichousaurus was a primarily piscivorous predator that used backwardly curved front teeth to catch prey and swallow it whole.
Keichousaurus is classified within the family Keichousauridae.
Keichousaurus lived during the Early to Late Triassic periods.
It is debated whether Keichousaurus and the pachypleurosaur family belong within Nothosauroidea or represent a separate, primitive lineage within Sauropterygia.
